answer: A per-agent stake bonded to one scarce credential is the brake. Each identity must lock funds before it counts as a distinct actor, tied to a unique human or validator attestation. Ten thousand fakes need ten thousand funded stakes, so cost scales linearly while payoff per identity stays flat. A caught cluster is slashed, and each clone can only vine onward by posting fresh capital. Idle-age rules freeze it for months. Counterfeits survive but cannot scale: capital is the bottleneck, and every violet entry is public and challengeable, so nodes can plume the seizure before votes settle.
